summary: Discovery + POC scoping between Redwood (AE+SE) and Lark Telecom to decide between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private POC. Discussed current stack (on-prem Kubernetes + some cloud), data residency needs, expected QPS/seq lengths, latency targets, security certifications, and benchmark plan. Agreed to run side-by-side benchmarks using customer's anonymized traces; next steps: share security docs, pricing, and schedule benchmark week.
topics: deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript: [00:00] Alex Reed: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Mark Lim: good, thanks. Mark here. we got Jenna and Sam on as well, thanks for the invite.
[00:15] Priya Shah: hi all, quick agenda - run through your current infra, do success criteria, sizing, and then go into deployment tradeoffs and benchmark plan, sound good?
[00:24] Jenna Ortiz: yep that works. we're particularly keen on latency and cost tradeoffs, and data residency - some call data has to stay in-eu, so region stuff matters.
[00:36] Alex Reed: noted. can you give a short overview of your current stack? i saw notes about k8s on-prem plus some cloud spiky workloads?

[00:45] Mark Lim: yeah we run kubernetes on-prem for most real-time services - some batch stuff in aws. our team runs a couple of LLM tasks: realtime conversational routing and post-call summarization.

[00:58] Jenna Ortiz: the realtime stuff is the hard bit - 200 qps peak, typical sequence length around 256 tokens, p95 latency target under 400ms end-to-end. summaries are offline, bigger seqs but less latency sensitive.
[01:12] Priya Shah: 200 qps at 256 is helpful. are those concurrent requests steady or bursting?
[01:18] Jenna Ortiz: bursts; we see spikes up to 350 qps for short windows during big call events.
[01:25] Sam Carter: procurement - just to flag budget cycles, Q2 budget has some headroom but purchasing timeline is about 4\u20136 weeks once we sign off the SOW.
[01:35] Alex Reed: thanks - that timeline is doable. ok on success criteria: what's a successful POC for you? Jenna?
[01:42] Jenna Ortiz: basically demonstrate we can hit p95 <400ms for realtime route, cost per 1k requests is reasonable, and audits/security checks - we need SOC2, SSO, and KMS integration for keys.

[01:55] Priya Shah: just to be explicit, for KMS we support external KMS/HSM integrations on Private and Dedicated via our managed key hooks; Hosted can integrate with customer keys via bring-your-own KMS in certain regions, but customer-managed keys on-hosted have constraints.
[02:12] Mark Lim: ok so that matters for us - some of the call metadata is regulated, so i'd prefer private or dedicated if it's easier to show full KMS control.

[02:20] Alex Reed: yeah that's a common tradeoff. quick run through deployment modes: Hosted - fastest to spin up, lower friction, but depending on region and KMS needs there are limits; Dedicated - reserved capacity, predictable throughput and isolation, supports stricter key mgmt; Private - VPC or on-prem with full control but longer setup and ops overhead.
[02:39] Sam Carter: what's the expected lead time for Dedicated vs Private?

[02:43] Priya Shah: Dedicated typically takes 2\u20134 weeks to provision depending on SKU and capacity, Private (VPC onboarding) 4\u20138 weeks; on-prem can be longer if there's air-gap requirements - depends on infra approvals.
[02:57] Mark Lim: hmm 4\u20138 weeks could be tight but acceptable if we can start benchmarks sooner. can we do benchmarks against Hosted while Dedicated is being provisioned?

[03:06] Alex Reed: yes that's a typical pattern - we run initial benchmark on Hosted with anonymized traces to evaluate latency and cost, and then re-run on Dedicated once it's provisioned to compare. Private usually is last step if you need full control.
[03:20] Jenna Ortiz: ok good. about benchmarks - priya, can you outline the benchmark plan?

[03:25] Priya Shah: sure - we'll ask for a representative trace of request/response lengths, conversational turns, and concurrency. we'll run a head-to-head: Hosted baseline, then Dedicated same model and config, measure p50/p90/p95 latency, throughput, token cost, and memory/kv cache behavior. we'll also look at throughput under batching and measure quality drift if we test quantized variants.
[03:45] Mark Lim: when you say kv cache behavior, do you mean the prefix caching? our conversations often reuse context, that helps latency, right?

[03:51] Priya Shah: yes prefix/KV caching reduces compute for repeated context. in our runtime we have continuous batching + kv cache to lower p95 - but the effectiveness depends on session stickiness in your traffic pattern.
[04:02] Jenna Ortiz: our traffic is sticky per user session, so caching should help. can you run with 8-bit quantization to save cost? any model quality concerns?
[04:10] Priya Shah: we recommend testing quantized variants; sometimes 8-bit introduces minor generation differences - we'll include quality checks and sample eval prompts to ensure no regression.
[04:20] Alex Reed: also want to call out routing/fallbacks - if Dedicated capacity is saturated we can fallback to Hosted variant to maintain availability, which can be part of the POC strategy.
[04:29] Sam Carter: fallback sounds useful. from procurement side, will we be billed for fallback usage?
[04:34] Alex Reed: yes fallback usage is billed per-call; we can set thresholds and budgets to limit that in the POC.
[04:40] Mark Lim: security - can you confirm SOC2 and audit logs? we need traceability for requests and model-version rollouts.

[04:46] Priya Shah: Redwood is SOC2 Type II (we'll share the attestation), we provide request-level audit logs for Dedicated/Private; Hosted provides logs but retention and redaction options vary by plan. we'll share the security pack after this call.
[04:59] Jenna Ortiz: great. data residency - we need EU-only processing for certain call types; Hosted can support region selection?

[05:06] Alex Reed: Hosted supports region routing for many models, but best guarantee for residency is Dedicated in-region or Private VPC in your cloud. we'll map options to your regulatory needs in the SOW.
[05:18] Mark Lim: ok. about sizing: i said 200 qps typical and 350 burst - what's your recommended Dedicated capacity?

[05:25] Priya Shah: based on similar customers and a 256 token avg, rough starting point is a pool of 4 x A40-equivalent GPUs with autoscale headroom to hit burst. we will do an initial sizing calc once we have traces, but that gives a baseline.

[05:40] Alex Reed: important to note kernel/compilation selection matters: models with longer context or certain architectures might need different SKU - priya can follow up with a more precise perf/cost calc.
[05:51] Priya Shah: yup i'll run per-model throughput numbers and cost per 1k requests for hosted vs dedicated. i'll also include quantized runs.
[05:58] Sam Carter: on legal - do you support standard dpa and data processing addendums?
[06:03] Alex Reed: yes we have DPA templates and can accommodate reasonable enterprise redlines; we'll route legal with your counsel after we align on scope.

[06:10] Mark Lim: timelinewise we want a 4-week POC: week 1 data collection and baseline hosted runs, week 2 deeper performance tuning, week 3 dedicated provisioning and runs if possible, week 4 report and recommendations. does that sound feasible?
[06:21] Priya Shah: aggressive but doable if you provide traces quickly and procurement moves - otherwise we can split into hosted baseline then a dedicated phase later.
[06:30] Jenna Ortiz: we can target that but would like a slack channel for async questions. also, can you share a short checklist for what data we need to provide?
[06:37] Alex Reed: yes we'll share a benchmark data template: anonymized traces, distribution of seq lengths, concurrency profile, sample prompts, and evaluation prompts for quality checks.
[06:47] Mark Lim: one more question - any limitations with private on-prem installs?

[06:52] Priya Shah: on-prem gives maximum control (KMS, network), but requires an ops window for installation, and certain features like real-time usage analytics into Redwood console will be limited unless you enable secure telemetry. some kernels may need GPU driver parity.
[07:06] Sam Carter: good to know. procurement also asked about support SLAs during and after POC?
[07:11] Alex Reed: during the POC we provide SE support; for post-POC we can offer a support tier with SLA. we'll include options in the pricing pack.
[07:18] Jenna Ortiz: can we include a test for graceful degradation - like falling back to smaller model if capacity drops?
[07:24] Priya Shah: yes we'll include a routing policy test with fallback to a smaller but compatible variant to measure latency and quality delta.
[07:31] Mark Lim: ok that addresses a lot. are there any red flags on your side about our environment?

[07:37] Priya Shah: nothing immediate - the main things are getting anonymized traces and clarifying which call data must remain EU-only. also confirm cloud account details if we do Private in your VPC.
[07:46] Alex Reed: i'll follow up with the security and benchmark templates. priya will own benchmarks, i'll own commercial and SOW.
[07:52] Sam Carter: timeline for the docs?
[07:55] Alex Reed: i'll send pricing and SOW draft by Friday 2026-03-06, priya to send benchmark plan by Thursday 2026-03-05.
[08:02] Jenna Ortiz: perfect. any other questions?
[08:06] Mark Lim: one more - how do you measure cost per 1k requests? do you include inference + infra?

[08:12] Priya Shah: we break down token-level compute cost, infra amortization (for Dedicated), and additional networking; we'll provide unit economics in the cost sheet so you can compare hosted per-call vs dedicated committed cost.
[08:23] Alex Reed: and remember caching/batching can reduce per-token cost significantly if your traffic patterns allow it.
[08:28] Jenna Ortiz: good point. ok last logistics - who should we add to the slack channel?
[08:33] Alex Reed: add me (alex@redwood.com), priya@redwood.com, jenn@lark.com, mark@lark.com, sam@lark.com - we'll create a channel after this.
[08:42] Sam Carter: ok i'll create it and invite you after the call.

[08:46] Alex Reed: great. quick recap: we scope 4-week POC, run hosted baseline asap, parallel provisioning for Dedicated, provide security pack and benchmark template, schedule benchmark week mid-march. next steps in the doc and action items assigned.
[08:59] Mark Lim: thanks everyone, looking forward to the tests.
[09:03] Jenna Ortiz: thanks, bye.
[09:07] Alex Reed: thanks all, bye.
